meta.topic: uv shorts — uv pip compile prints and writes nothing without -o
meta.onePayoff: Every pip command works with uv in front, compile prints unless you pass -o, and uv is deliberately stricter.
meta.openLoop: If the commands are the same, what actually changes?
meta.analogy: One parcel, two gates: pip waves it through, uv stamps it with the reason.

seo.title: The uv command that prints instead of writing #python #pip
seo.description: uv pip compile prints to your screen and creates no file unless you pass -o. Catches almost everybody once.

scenes.narration: You already know pip. Put uv in front and every command still works.
Same flags, same arguments, same shape of output. The install that took pip eleven seconds takes under a second and a half here.

uvStage.headline: Put [uv] in front of it
uvStage.premise: The pip interface is deliberately familiar. Same flags, same shapes, faster.

steps.label: uv pip install rich
steps.detail: same command, one word in front

scenes.narration: But here is a trap that catches almost everybody. uv pip compile prints its output. It writes no file at all unless you pass dash o.

uvStage.headline: It [prints]. It does not write.
uvStage.premise: Without -o the compiled output goes to your screen, and no file is created.

steps.label: ls requirements.txt
out: ls: cannot access requirements.txt: No such file
steps.detail: exactly as promised, and as surprising

scenes.narration: And uv is deliberately stricter. Broken metadata that pip waves straight through, uv refuses — and tells you exactly why, now rather than in three weeks.

uvStage.headline: uv stops what [pip waves] through
uvStage.premise: The same package, offered to both. Only one of them reads the small print.

stage.label: uv
stage.detail: stricter, and it tells you now

scenes.narration: Every pip command translated in the full course.
